review: Fourth independent power, cable, receiver and transport review
scope: Requirements and implementation-status audit; no CAD mutation, no new DRC run, no hardware powered or tested.

records.title: Actual power demand and thermal limit
records.evidence: The 4.981 W nominal allocation and 0.60 A cable ceiling are design assumptions. The preceding corner analysis leaves only 16.32 mV core margin at 3 A before copper, ripple and transients. No application estimate or powered measurement exists.
records.closure_criterion: Freeze the FPGA order code and implemented utilization/activity; run power estimation, PDN/DC-drop and thermal analysis; then record worst-case rail/load-step/temperature measurements in the actual mated assembly.
records.proposed_owner: FPGA designer and power/layout engineer; lab for final measurement
records.external_dependency: Actual acquisition/stimulation modes, enclosure/airflow and maximum ambient must come from the system owner; estimates/design can continue now.

records.title: Cable source protection and input transients
records.evidence: Both native manifests connect J4.19 directly to LINK_12V and converter inputs. Carrier eFuse, UVLO and proposed headboard damping are absent. TPS259540/3.16 kΩ is a candidate, not a demonstrated 0.60–0.75 A limit.
records.closure_criterion: Build the protection/UVLO/slew circuit into the carrier and final headboard; calculate tolerance/fault pulses and minimum input capacitance, then validate startup, brownout, short circuit and permitted mating procedure.
records.external_dependency: No new user decision needed for design; selected components and a physical cable/source are needed to qualify it.

records.title: Exact cable, connector and shared return path
records.evidence: J4 is still a Molex family placeholder. Contacts 4/7/10/13/16 and shell are all GND. Parallel ground/shield paths make a single-return 90 mV example non-predictive; loop resistance does not by itself set common-mode ground shift.
records.closure_criterion: Freeze both connector order codes and a contact-by-contact cable drawing; verify pair topology, polarity, impedance/skew, current/temperature rating and measured feed/return resistance/inductance, including shield and ASIC-board return paths.
records.external_dependency: Supplier cable data and the complete grounded assembly are required; the short custom cable remains a proposal.

records.title: LVDS receiver bias and termination
records.evidence: Maximum Artix-7 LVDS_25 output common mode equals the AU25P HP DC input limit at 1.425 V; positive remote ground offset has no guaranteed allowance at this corner. Failure of a real unit has not been demonstrated. AC coupling is only a candidate.
records.closure_criterion: Select and implement a qualified common-mode solution. For AC coupling, cover all four pairs with bias/termination values, attributes, leakage, high-pass/baseline-wander, startup/clock-loss and powered/unpowered voltage checks; validate signal integrity.
records.external_dependency: Design work is internal; cable and hardware measurements are later closure evidence.

records.title: Exact XEM contact map and clock resources
records.evidence: Bank64/VIO1 is only a bank-level proposal. The official map provides GC P/N choices MC1 25/27 (AD20/AE20), 37/39 (AD21/AE21), 41/43 (AB21/AC21), 45/47 (AC19/AD19). No lane/contact/polarity XDC or timing result is committed.
records.closure_criterion: Choose clock/data pins and receive architecture; add module PCB plus package delay to carrier/cable/headboard budgets; implement XDC and pass placement, clocking, CDC and timing in both FPGAs.
records.external_dependency: No user pin-selection question is necessary; an engineering choice and tool verification are needed.

records.title: VIO configuration, power-loss and startup interlock
records.evidence: Bank64 defaults to 1.0 V; setting 180 and a power cycle are required for proposed 1.8 V. BOARD_READY remains asserted after initialization and is not a continuous rail monitor. PWR GOOD excludes VIOx. No receiver interlock is implemented.
records.closure_criterion: Provide measured/verified target power and expected VIO settings, startup/train enable, clock-loss recovery and fail-safe state for every source-on/destination-off case; include reconfiguration and USB disconnect.
records.external_dependency: Device firmware/settings and bench power-sequencing tests are required; do not infer them from the indicator LEDs.

records.title: ASIC power distribution and cross-board signal safety
records.evidence: The proposed mezzanines have 117 signals, three reserved contacts and ground blades; no ASIC supply contacts. VCC_ASIC_1V5 names FPGA I/O-bank power and does not establish that the ASICs are powered from it. Independently powered ASIC outputs can drive an unpowered FPGA and vice versa.
records.closure_criterion: Define ASIC/routing-board supply source, voltage tolerances, peak currents and ground bonds; verify simultaneous and independent shutdown/startup, input clamps and default reset/stimulation states; add isolation or sequencing where required.
records.external_dependency: Actual ASIC power/IO limits and intended routing-board power source are external inputs. Existing 1.5 V historical wiring is not a substitute.

records.title: Remote JTAG and runtime command contract
records.evidence: Existing JTAG wires reach the target, but XEM fabric GPIO master, BSCAN command endpoint, arbitration and recovery are not implemented. The 1.8 V rail revision and 3.3 V core need different voltage handling; static JTAG needs its own margin budget.
records.closure_criterion: Implement boot/programming path plus command framing, acknowledgment, error/retry, timestamp/latency and reset/watchdog behavior. Demonstrate programming and acquisition can coexist or define allowed interruption. Choose drive/level handling and a verified return/noise budget.
records.external_dependency: ASIC owner must specify command functions and any bounded stimulation latency; HDL/protocol design does not require the user to select pins.

records.title: Wire protocol and per-lane encoding
records.evidence: The 3×800 Mbit/s, 8b/10b, 400 MHz DDR-clock scheme is arithmetic, not HDL. Byte striping must preserve each lane's running disparity. The 20-byte metadata allocation, synchronization and CRC are not frozen. Raw 16-bit-per-sample forwarding exceeds the 240 MB/s encoded capacity.
records.closure_criterion: Specify bit/sample order, 12-bit extraction, lane order/polarity, comma/training/idle, lane deskew, timestamp/CRC and loss recovery; simulate corrupted/lost/restarted data, then close timing and measure eye/BER for the final assembly.
records.external_dependency: ASIC frame/clock behavior is required from its owner. The remaining packet design is an internal engineering task.

records.title: USB frame packing and clock crossing
records.evidence: The proposed 6,165-byte link frame is 1 mod 4 and 5 mod 16. XEM USB3 pipes use 32-bit FPGA words and host lengths divisible by 16; a frame cannot be passed as one 6,165-byte Pipe read. okHost uses 100.8 MHz, separate from link clocks.
records.closure_criterion: Implement a documented continuous-byte repacker/aggregation or receiver-side padding, asynchronous FIFO and parser. Test frames crossing every word/USB block boundary, resets and short/error returns; pin the SDK/HDL versions and use supported Classic endpoints.
records.external_dependency: No user decision is needed; choose and verify the transport contract. Padding at the receiver does not need to change the physical link.

records.title: Backpressure, bounded buffering and overflow
records.status: unresolved system requirement and absent implementation
records.evidence: All four fast pairs run headboard→XEM. USB block throttling does not stop incoming ASIC samples. At 192.65625 MB/s, a 100 ms no-drain interval needs 19.265625 MB; 2 GiB is only 11.1467 s as an ideal all-memory upper bound before reserves. No bounded-stall/overflow policy is present.
records.closure_criterion: Choose a maximum supported stall and usable DDR ring size; implement watermark, loss counters and explicit stop/drop behavior. Prove host stalls, USB disconnect and disk-full never silently corrupt or relabel data. Do not assume ASIC clocks can be paused safely.
records.proposed_owner: System owner sets behavior; receiver/host engineer implements it
records.external_dependency: Whether acquisition may pause or must report dropped samples and the required uninterrupted recording window are system requirements; actual ASIC pause behavior belongs to ASIC owner.

records.title: Actual PC-to-disk throughput and recording size
records.evidence: The link arithmetic does not validate the chosen computer, USB hub/controller, SDK version or storage. Compact framing is 192.65625 MB/s and 693.5625 GB per hour, before filesystem/container overhead; 16-bit sample storage is larger.
records.closure_criterion: Run continuous patterned acquisition on the intended PC/port/disk for the required duration with CRC, sequence/overrun counters and simultaneous commands; document negotiated USB speed and measured margin, latency, disk-full/disconnect recovery.
records.external_dependency: The intended recording computer/disk and required duration must eventually be identified. Synthetic software/FPGA validation can proceed meanwhile.
